EXPERIMENTAL SYSTEMS
OBSERVATION · INTENTION · DESIGN
01 / THE SUBJECT

The developing Alchemy perception portfolio looks toward motion analysis, object relations, pose and landmark providers, provider-neutral feature contracts and portable compute.

01 / 03

Sequence gives meaning

A single frame can mislead. Temporal tracking and semantic relationships can help distinguish an observation from a conclusion about activity or intention.

  • Temporal evidence and tracks
  • Spatial and geometric context
  • Observable changes
02 / 03

Provider-neutral perception

Pose, hand landmarks, facial mesh and comparable features should be served through separate library and service contracts. Provider implementations may vary, without rewriting the application around one SDK.

  • Landmark and feature contracts
  • Replaceable inference providers
  • Canonical evidence projections
03 / 03

Compute where it belongs

Media processing can be expensive. Job-to-node admission, compute placement and storage pins should let a task travel within an MI/MU mesh while its inputs, state and results remain durable.

  • Portable execution definitions
  • Declared resource requirements
  • Auditable outputs
